he was bond, whether he ſhould proſper temporally or no ; but that he vowed things which
particular godlie workes, to which he was not otherwiſe obliged. As here are not other-
he expreſſeth two things. Preſuppoſing befoie al, that the Lord Omnipotent wiſe comman:
ſhal be his God, he addeth, firſt And this ſtone, vvhich I haue erected for a title, ded.
shal be called the houſe cod. wherby he promiſed the building of a Church,
performed at his returne ( chap. 35. ) Secondly he added, And of al things vyhich
thou shalt geue me t vvil offer tithes to thee. And this Likwiſe was of free deuotion.
ben. 14. For tithes alſo in the law of nature were dew to Prieſts, and by inferior Prieſts
to the chiefe Prieſt, as Abraham gaue tithes to Melchiſedech. And ſo al his
tithes were dew to his father, and after his tather him ſelfe was chicfe: yet
he promiſed them to Cod, that is, to offer them in Sacrifice, and beſtow them
in other vſes pertaining to Gods ſeruice.
CHAP. XXIX.
Iacob intertained by Laban, 15. ſerueth him ſeuen yeares for gachel, 23. buſ
firſt receiuing Lia, 27. ſeuen dayes after receiueth alſo Rachel, and ſerueth
for her ſeuen yeares more. 31. She remaining barren, Lia beareth foure
ſonnes.
† †Aco therfore going on his iourney, came into the Eaſt
countrie. † And he ſawe a wel in the field, and three
flockes of sheepe lying beſide it : for of it the beaſts were
watered, and the mouth therof was cloſed with a great ſtone.
† And the maner was when al the sheepe were geathered
togeather they did rowle of the ſtone, and after the sheepe
were refreshed they put it on the mouth of the wel againe.
† And he ſaid to the sheperds: Brethren,, Whence are
you ? Who anſwered : Of Haran. † And he asked them,
ſaying : Rnow you Laban the ſonne of Nachor? They ſaid :
We do knowe him. † Is he in health? quoth he : He is in
